plan.title: MyFriends
plan.description:
A mobile app for finding and connecting with people nearby who are open to making
new friends. Not dating. The premise is that adults and older teenagers who move
to a new city, change jobs, or come out of a long relationship have no good way to
meet people platonically, and existing apps either optimise for romance or for
professional networking.

## Product

A person installs the app, creates a profile, and sets themselves as open to new
friends. The app shows other people nearby who are also open, ordered by how well
their stated interests and availability match. Either person can send a connection
request; when both accept, they can message each other in the app.

The distinguishing feature is the "open to new friends" toggle. Discovery only
surfaces people who have deliberately turned it on, so nobody appears in anyone
else's results by default.

## Users

- Adults aged 18 and over, the primary audience.
- Older teenagers aged 16 and 17, who we expect to be a meaningful minority of
  signups and who we do not want to exclude.

## Platforms

Native on both platforms, no cross-platform framework.

- iOS: Swift, SwiftUI, minimum iOS 16.
- Android: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, minimum API 29.
- A shared backend serving both clients.

The business logic that decides matching and eligibility should be testable
independently of the UI on each platform.

## Markets at launch

United Kingdom, the European Union (starting with Ireland, Germany and the
Netherlands), and the United States (California first).

criteria.text: A person can create an account and a profile containing a display name, a photo, an age, a short bio, and up to ten interest tags.
A person can turn "open to new friends" on and off, and turning it off removes them from every other person's discovery results within one minute.
Discovery returns only people who currently have "open to new friends" turned on and who are within the searching person's chosen radius, which can be set to 1, 5, 10 or 25 kilometres.
Discovery results are ordered by a match score computed from shared interest tags and overlapping stated availability, and the app shows the person why each result was surfaced.
A person can send a connection request to someone in their discovery results, and can send at most twenty requests in any twenty-four hour period.
Two people can exchange messages in the app only after both have accepted the connection.
A person can block another person, and a blocked person can never appear in their discovery results, send them a request, or message them.
A person can report another person or a message, choosing from a fixed list of reasons and optionally adding free text.
The app works with no network connection to the extent of showing the person's own profile and their existing accepted connections and previously loaded messages.
The iOS and Android clients share a single definition of the match score, so the same two profiles produce the same score on both platforms.
The backend exposes the discovery, request, and messaging operations over an authenticated API, and rejects any unauthenticated call.
Location is only read while the person is actively using the app.

plan.constitution_md:
# Engineering constitution

The governing principles for every plan and every build in this repository.
PFactory reads this file during planning, surfaces it for human approval, and
turns the clauses marked enforceable into hard checks.

Principles are numbered. A principle marked **(enforceable)** is not advice: a
plan that violates it does not pass the gates, and the only way past is a
recorded waiver with a named approver.

## P1: The person owns their data

- **P1 (enforceable):** every feature that stores information about a person must state how long it is kept and what deletes it. "Indefinitely" is an answer, but it has to be written down.

## P2: Deletion is a feature, not a support ticket

- **P2 (enforceable):** a person can delete their account and their content from inside the app, without contacting anyone, and the deletion path is built in the same phase as the feature that creates the data.

## P3: We know who is a child

- **P3 (enforceable):** any feature reachable by someone under 18 must state its age-assurance mechanism and what changes for a minor. Collecting a birth date is not an age-assurance mechanism.

## P4: Location is borrowed, never taken

- **P4 (enforceable):** location is read only with explicit consent, only at the precision the feature actually needs, and never in the background unless the plan says why and the person was told.

## P5: Every place people can reach each other needs a way out

- **P5 (enforceable):** any person-to-person surface ships with blocking, reporting, and a stated response path in the same phase. A social feature without moderation is not shippable.

## P6: The plan names its jurisdictions

- **P6 (enforceable):** a plan that processes personal data names the markets it launches in, because the obligations differ and we cannot infer them.

## P7: We do not claim what we did not test

- **P7 (enforceable):** a verification lane that could not run is reported as not run, with the reason. It is never reported as passed and never quietly omitted.

## P8: The store is part of the product

- Apple App Review and Google Play policy are requirements, not paperwork at the end. Anything that would be rejected is a defect found late.

## P9: Both platforms behave the same

- Where iOS and Android implement the same rule, the rule has one definition and one set of tests. Two implementations of the same logic will diverge.

## P10: Accessibility is in the acceptance criteria

- VoiceOver and TalkBack are part of "done" for any screen, not a later pass.
plan.raw_text:
# MyFriends

A mobile app for finding and connecting with people nearby who are open to making
new friends. Not dating. The premise is that adults and older teenagers who move
to a new city, change jobs, or come out of a long relationship have no good way to
meet people platonically, and existing apps either optimise for romance or for
professional networking.

## Product

A person installs the app, creates a profile, and sets themselves as open to new
friends. The app shows other people nearby who are also open, ordered by how well
their stated interests and availability match. Either person can send a connection
request; when both accept, they can message each other in the app.

The distinguishing feature is the "open to new friends" toggle. Discovery only
surfaces people who have deliberately turned it on, so nobody appears in anyone
else's results by default.

## Users

- Adults aged 18 and over, the primary audience.
- Older teenagers aged 16 and 17, who we expect to be a meaningful minority of
  signups and who we do not want to exclude.

## Platforms

Native on both platforms, no cross-platform framework.

- iOS: Swift, SwiftUI, minimum iOS 16.
- Android: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, minimum API 29.
- A shared backend serving both clients.

The business logic that decides matching and eligibility should be testable
independently of the UI on each platform.

## Markets at launch

United Kingdom, the European Union (starting with Ireland, Germany and the
Netherlands), and the United States (California first).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A person can create an account and a profile containing a display name, a photo, an age, a short bio, and up to ten interest tags.
- A person can turn "open to new friends" on and off, and turning it off removes them from every other person's discovery results within one minute.
- Discovery returns only people who currently have "open to new friends" turned on and who are within the searching person's chosen radius, which can be set to 1, 5, 10 or 25 kilometres.
- Discovery results are ordered by a match score computed from shared interest tags and overlapping stated availability, and the app shows the person why each result was surfaced.
- A person can send a connection request to someone in their discovery results, and can send at most twenty requests in any twenty-four hour period.
- Two people can exchange messages in the app only after both have accepted the connection.
- A person can block another person, and a blocked person can never appear in their discovery results, send them a request, or message them.
- A person can report another person or a message, choosing from a fixed list of reasons and optionally adding free text.
- The app works with no network connection to the extent of showing the person's own profile and their existing accepted connections and previously loaded messages.
- The iOS and Android clients share a single definition of the match score, so the same two profiles produce the same score on both platforms.
- The backend exposes the discovery, request, and messaging operations over an authenticated API, and rejects any unauthenticated call.
- Location is only read while the person is actively using the app.

acceptance_criteria: A person can create an account and a profile containing a display name, a photo, an age, a short bio, and up to ten interest tags.
The app has a complete store listing (name, description, screenshots, privacy details) that complies with App Store and Play Store review policies.
Each runtime permission (location, notifications, camera, contacts) is requested in context, when the feature needing it is first used, with a rationale shown.
The app remains usable offline and on a poor network: cached content is shown and failed actions surface a retry.
Deep links / universal links open the correct in-app screen, including from a cold start.
Crash reporting is wired and symbolicated so production crashes are attributable to a release.
Core flows are operable with VoiceOver (iOS) and TalkBack (Android), with labels on every interactive element.
App size and battery budgets are stated and met: a download-size cap and no abnormal background battery drain.
Releases ship through a release channel with a staged rollout (TestFlight / Play internal testing, then a percentage rollout).
A forced-upgrade path exists: a minimum supported app version can be enforced remotely with an upgrade prompt.

# Testing Strategy — MyFriends

> Plan: `013-myfriends` · Plan type: `mobile-app`

## Overview

Layered testing strategy for this plan. Tests are organised into lanes; each acceptance criterion is mapped to the lane and approach that best verifies it. Test generation and execution hand over to TFactory.

## Test Lanes & Coverage Targets

| Lane | Coverage target | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unit | 80% line / 70% branch | Pure functions, modules, and edge cases in isolation. |
| integration | Critical paths covered | Component boundaries, persistence, and external collaborators (stubbed or containerised). |
| e2e | All happy paths + key failures | End-to-end user / API journeys against a running stack. |

## Acceptance Criteria → Test Approach

| AC | Criterion | Test approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AC#1` | A person can create an account and a profile containing a display name, a photo, an age, a short bio, and up to ten interest tags. | unit — assert behaviour directly with focused cases |
| `AC#2` | A person can turn "open to new friends" on and off, and turning it off removes them from every other person's discovery results within one minute. | unit — assert behaviour directly with focused cases |
| `AC#3` | Discovery returns only people who currently have "open to new friends" turned on and who are within the searching person's chosen radius, which can be set to 1, 5, 10 or 25 kilometres. | unit — assert behaviour directly with focused cases |
| `AC#4` | Discovery results are ordered by a match score computed from shared interest tags and overlapping stated availability, and the app shows the person why each result was surfaced. | unit — assert behaviour directly with focused cases |
| `AC#5` | A person can send a connection request to someone in their discovery results, and can send at most twenty requests in any twenty-four hour period. | unit — assert behaviour directly with focused cases |
| `AC#6` | Two people can exchange messages in the app only after both have accepted the connection. | unit — assert behaviour directly with focused cases |
| `AC#7` | A person can block another person, and a blocked person can never appear in their discovery results, send them a request, or message them. | unit — assert behaviour directly with focused cases |
| `AC#8` | A person can report another person or a message, choosing from a fixed list of reasons and optionally adding free text. | unit — assert behaviour directly with focused cases |
| `AC#9` | The app works with no network connection to the extent of showing the person's own profile and their existing accepted connections and previously loaded messages. | unit — assert behaviour directly with focused cases |
| `AC#10` | The iOS and Android clients share a single definition of the match score, so the same two profiles produce the same score on both platforms. | unit — assert behaviour directly with focused cases |
| `AC#11` | The backend exposes the discovery, request, and messaging operations over an authenticated API, and rejects any unauthenticated call. | integration — exercise the boundary with a real/stubbed collaborator |
| `AC#12` | Location is only read while the person is actively using the app. | unit — assert behaviour directly with focused cases |

## Definition of Done

- Every acceptance criterion above has at least one passing test.
- Coverage targets per lane are met or explicitly waived with a reason.
- New tests run in CI and gate the build.

# CI/CD Pipeline — MyFriends

> Plan: `013-myfriends` · Plan type: `mobile-app`

## Overview

Continuous integration and delivery pipeline for this plan. The pipeline runs on every push and pull request; deploy stages are gated on a green build of all preceding stages.

## Stages

1. **lint** — Static analysis and formatting checks; fail fast on style or type errors.
2. **test** — Run the full automated test suite; require all lanes green and publish the coverage report.
3. **build** — Compile / bundle the application and produce versioned build artifacts.
4. **security scan** — Scan dependencies and (if built) the container image for known vulnerabilities; fail on findings above the agreed threshold.
5. **deploy** — Promote the build artifacts to the target environment after manual approval; verify the deployment is healthy.

## Gating

- Each stage depends on a green result from the previous stage.
- Deploy stages require manual approval and run only on the default branch.

## Acceptance Criteria Coverage

The pipeline must keep these plan acceptance criteria green:

- `AC#1` — A person can create an account and a profile containing a display name, a photo, an age, a short bio, and up to ten interest tags.
- `AC#2` — A person can turn "open to new friends" on and off, and turning it off removes them from every other person's discovery results within one minute.
- `AC#3` — Discovery returns only people who currently have "open to new friends" turned on and who are within the searching person's chosen radius, which can be set to 1, 5, 10 or 25 kilometres.
- `AC#4` — Discovery results are ordered by a match score computed from shared interest tags and overlapping stated availability, and the app shows the person why each result was surfaced.
- `AC#5` — A person can send a connection request to someone in their discovery results, and can send at most twenty requests in any twenty-four hour period.
- `AC#6` — Two people can exchange messages in the app only after both have accepted the connection.
- `AC#7` — A person can block another person, and a blocked person can never appear in their discovery results, send them a request, or message them.
- `AC#8` — A person can report another person or a message, choosing from a fixed list of reasons and optionally adding free text.
- `AC#9` — The app works with no network connection to the extent of showing the person's own profile and their existing accepted connections and previously loaded messages.
- `AC#10` — The iOS and Android clients share a single definition of the match score, so the same two profiles produce the same score on both platforms.
- `AC#11` — The backend exposes the discovery, request, and messaging operations over an authenticated API, and rejects any unauthenticated call.
- `AC#12` — Location is only read while the person is actively using the app.

annotation.improved_markdown:
# MyFriends

A mobile app for finding and connecting with people nearby who are open to making
new friends. Not dating. The premise is that adults and older teenagers who move
to a new city, change jobs, or come out of a long relationship have no good way to
meet people platonically, and existing apps either optimise for romance or for
professional networking.

## Product

A person installs the app, creates a profile, and sets themselves as open to new
friends. The app shows other people nearby who are also open, ordered by how well
their stated interests and availability match. Either person can send a connection
request; when both accept, they can message each other in the app.

The distinguishing feature is the "open to new friends" toggle. Discovery only
surfaces people who have deliberately turned it on, so nobody appears in anyone
else's results by default.

## Users

- Adults aged 18 and over, the primary audience.
- Older teenagers aged 16 and 17, who we expect to be a meaningful minority of
  signups and who we do not want to exclude.

## Platforms

Native on both platforms, no cross-platform framework.

- iOS: Swift, SwiftUI, minimum iOS 16.
- Android: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, minimum API 29.
- A shared backend serving both clients.

The business logic that decides matching and eligibility should be testable
independently of the UI on each platform.

## Markets at launch

United Kingdom, the European Union (starting with Ireland, Germany and the
Netherlands), and the United States (California first).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A person can create an account and a profile containing a display name, a photo, an age, a short bio, and up to ten interest tags.
- A person can turn "open to new friends" on and off, and turning it off removes them from every other person's discovery results within one minute.
- Discovery returns only people who currently have "open to new friends" turned on and who are within the searching person's chosen radius, which can be set to 1, 5, 10 or 25 kilometres.
- Discovery results are ordered by a match score computed from shared interest tags and overlapping stated availability, and the app shows the person why each result was surfaced.
- A person can send a connection request to someone in their discovery results, and can send at most twenty requests in any twenty-four hour period.
- Two people can exchange messages in the app only after both have accepted the connection.
- A person can block another person, and a blocked person can never appear in their discovery results, send them a request, or message them.
- A person can report another person or a message, choosing from a fixed list of reasons and optionally adding free text.
- The app works with no network connection to the extent of showing the person's own profile and their existing accepted connections and previously loaded messages.
- The iOS and Android clients share a single definition of the match score, so the same two profiles produce the same score on both platforms.
- The backend exposes the discovery, request, and messaging operations over an authenticated API, and rejects any unauthenticated call.
- Location is only read while the person is actively using the app.

---

## PFactory review — suggested edits

_The original above is unchanged. PFactory suggests the edits below; accept, reject, or adopt the improved version. Each cites why._

- **Why:** Unclear titles on: epic.

### 3. Lawful basis and purpose limitation not stated  `[medium]`

- **Source:** [GDPR Art. 5 - Principles relating to processing of personal data](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-5-gdpr/)

### 4. Location data handling not specified  `[high]`
- **Where:** line 17 — “surfaces people who have deliberately turned it on, so nobody appears in anyone”
- **Why:** location is read only with explicit consent, only at the precision the feature actually needs, and never in the background unless the plan says why and the person was told.
- **Source:** [Project constitution P4.1 (enforceable)](.factory/constitution.md)

### 5. Automated matching without profiling transparency  `[medium]`
- **Where:** line 17 — “surfaces people who have deliberately turned it on, so nobody appears in anyone”
- **Why:** Users must be told about automated decision-making, including profiling.
- **Source:** [GDPR Art. 13(2)(f) - Information to be provided](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-13-gdpr/)

### 6. User-to-user contact without trust and safety controls  `[high]`
- **Where:** line 42 — “## Acceptance Criteria”
- **Why:** any person-to-person surface ships with blocking, reporting, and a stated response path in the same phase. A social feature without moderation is not shippable.
- **Source:** [Project constitution P5.1 (enforceable)](.factory/constitution.md)

### 7. No retention or deletion policy stated  `[high]`
- **Where:** line 17 — “surfaces people who have deliberately turned it on, so nobody appears in anyone”
- **Why:** every feature that stores information about a person must state how long it is kept and what deletes it. "Indefinitely" is an answer, but it has to be written down.
- **Source:** [Project constitution P1.2 (enforceable)](.factory/constitution.md)

### 8. Store distribution without in-app account deletion  `[high]`
- **Where:** line 17 — “surfaces people who have deliberately turned it on, so nobody appears in anyone”
- **Why:** a person can delete their account and their content from inside the app, without contacting anyone, and the deletion path is built in the same phase as the feature that creates the data.
- **Source:** [Project constitution P2.1 (enforceable)](.factory/constitution.md)

### 9. No age assurance stated  `[high]`
- **Where:** line 17 — “surfaces people who have deliberately turned it on, so nobody appears in anyone”
- **Why:** any feature reachable by someone under 18 must state its age-assurance mechanism and what changes for a minor. Collecting a birth date is not an age-assurance mechanism.
- **Source:** [Project constitution P3.1 (enforceable)](.factory/constitution.md)

### 10. Unstated security / access scope  `[medium]`
- **Where:** line 40 — “Netherlands), and the United States (California first).”
- **Why:** A networked plan never states an authentication/authorization scope. Confirm access control is in scope (and how) or explicitly out of scope.
